newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - Road still rocky for LME copper.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - Road still rocky for LME copper.

text.p: The copper market looks set for more bumps this week as it rides out the end of a technical squeeze, analysts and traders said.
But the rollercoaster moves of last week -- when the cash to threes backwardation flared out to $270 -- are diminishing as tight dates fall off and the spread contracts.
"Once we pass the 28th of July, it calms down," a trader said, noting the traditionally slow summer season would follow the tight period.
Three months copper ended Friday's afternoon kerb stronger at $2,316 per tonne. Technical analysts said that, having hurdled resistance at $2,300, copper was now looking at the $2,350 level.
On the downside, the $2,250 area and last Thursday's low around $2,225 would cushion falls.
However, a softer cash/threes backwardation of $125/135 on Monday morning was also removing some of the market's underpinning and would continue to contract, traders said.
The other big feature which jolted the market last week was three consecutive days of big stock increases -- 17,025 tonnes on Wednesday and then 13,025 and 7,800 on subsequent days.
Traders said more metal was expected to flood into LME warehouses, attracted by the high backwardation, and left prices vulnerable to declines. Stocks rose by 3,250 tonnes on Monday morning.
"The final total may be close to 100,000 tonnes," brokers GNI said in a commentary.

"The deliveries are doing what they are supposed to do -- hitting the cash market rather than the three-month price -- for the moment. This cannot last and looked at dispassionately, the copper that is now being delivered is surplus material."
Most of the other metals drifted along with copper in unexceptional volumes and were feeling the dampening effect of the seasonal slowdown, traders said.
The exception had been zinc, which hurtled above the $1,500 mark last week, storming to new highs since September 1990 on bursts of fresh fund buying.
More gains were possible for the star performer of the complex, despite being overbought, analysts said.
Aluminium was taking copper's lead, with Friday's move above $1,607 setting up the next target at $1,620.
Tin had been the weakest in the complex, falling to 2-1/3 year lows last weak amid fund liquidation.
Targets below $5,400 were valid, analysts said.
